    IN THE MATTER OF EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY’S )
    ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                       ) Docket No. 26-0000062

       ORDER EXTENDING SUSPENSION PERIOD FOR ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317

          THIS MATTER comes before the Hearing Examiners upon their own motion. Being duly

informed, the Hearing Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE:

          1.      On March 27, 2026, El Paso Electric Company (“EPE”) filed its initial Application

for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (“Application”).

          2.      On April 2, 2026, the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”)

issued its Order Assigning Co-Hearing Examiners. 1 The Commission has since appointed

substitute Co-Hearing Examiners in this matter.2

          3.      On April 23, 2026, the Commission issued its Order Suspending Advice Notice No.

317, which suspended the implementation of EPE’s proposed rates for a period of nine-months,

starting on May 15, 2026.3 The initial suspension period therefore ended on February 15, 2027.

          4.      On July 16, 2026, Chief Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett issued a Sua Sponte

Order Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring the Filing of an

Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”). In the Sua Sponte Order, the Hearing Examiner


1
 See Order Appointing Co-Hearing Examiners and Amending Case Caption (April 2, 2026) at 3 (appointing
Co-Hearing Examiners Jocelyn Barrett and Elizabeth Hurst to oversee the matter).
2
 See Order Appointing Substitute Co-Hearing Examiner (July 20, 2026) at 2 (appointing Co-Hearing Examiner
Nicholas Rossi to substitute and replace Co-Hearing Examiner Elizabeth Hurst); see also Order Appointing
Substitute Co-Hearing Examiner (Aug. 19, 2026) at 2-3 (appointing Keven Gedko as Co-Hearing Examiner to
substitute and replace Co-Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett).
3
    Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 at 8.
 concluded that the Application was not filed in a sufficiently complete, accurate, and reviewable

form to permit the proceeding to continue fairly and efficiently.4 For these reasons, the Hearing

Examiner vacated the existing procedural schedule, tolled all pending motions and other deadlines,

required EPE to file a single amended and restated Application and complete supporting filing

package within 21 days of the issuance of the Sua Sponte Order, and required Staff to file a

completeness report within 7 days of EPE’s filing of its amended Application.5

           5.        On August 6, 2026, EPE filed its Amended Application for Revision of Retail

Electric Rates (“Amended Application”).

           6.        On August 12, 2026, the Public Interest Advocacy Staff (“Staff”) of the

Commission filed its Completeness Report, and concluded that “Staff has undertaken a good faith

effort to review EPE’s Amended Application, as directed by the Sua Sponte Order, and finds that

it is sufficiently complete to allow this matter to proceed.”6

           7.        On August 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued their Order Establishing

Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions, in which they stated their

agreement with the conclusion of Staff’s Completeness Report,7 and set new procedural deadlines

by which this matter will proceed, including a public hearing set for December 9, 2026 through

December 22, 2026.8




4
    Sua Sponte Order (July 16, 2026) at 1.
5

6
    Completeness Report (August 12, 2026) at 7.
7
    Order Establishing Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions (August 27, 2026) ¶ 5.
8
    Id. Decretal ¶ M.

Order Extending Suspension Period for Advice Notice No. 317
Page 2 of 3
           8.     The suspension period of Advice Notice No. 317 may be extended for an additional

three months if required.9

          9.     Given the revised procedural schedule for this matter, the Hearing Examiners find

that more time is required for the Commission to issue a final order in this docket, and therefore

an extension of the suspension period of Advice Notice No. 317 is required.

          10.    Accordingly, the suspension of Advice Notice No. 317 should be extended for an

additional period of two months, with the suspension period therefore ending on April 15, 2027.

          IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

          A.     The proposed rates filed by EPE in Advice Notice No. 317 are suspended for an

additional two months, until April 15, 2027.

ISSUED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on August 28, 2026.
